To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) μ-analysis is an approach allowing experimental determination of the order of formation (or assembly) of protein structural elements; (ii) μ-analysis is based on two types of experimental data: (a) the effect of single amino acid substitutions on the fluorescence of a multi-state fluorescent protein; (b) the effect of cysteine cross-linking on the fluorescence of the protein.
the formation of beta-hairs in the green fluorescent protein starts from the N-terminus, and proceeds in the direction of the C-terminus.
the order of formation and the structure of protein secondary elements can be experimentally determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to study the folding of multi-state proteins.
the development of a new experimental approach, μ-analysis, allowing the determination of the formation order of protein secondary structure elements in the process of protein folding.
the development of the μ-analysis approach, which allows the determination of the order of formation structural elements upon folding a multi-state protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the first formed elements of the protein structure are the beta-hairpins, and that they form in the following order: the first hairpin is formed by the residues 1–12 and 23–34, and then the second hairpin is formed from the residues 13–21 and 35–46.
the order of formation for beta-hairpins in GFP is as follows: 2-3-1-5-6-4.
in the case of the GFP folding, beta-hairpins are formed in the following order: beta-hairpins 3-4-5-6-1-2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the order of formation in the GFP is the following: 2 beta-hairpins, the beta-sheet, the beta-barrel, the 3 beta-hairpins and the 6th beta-hairpin.
the μ-analysis approach can be used to study the folding of any protein.
the order of formation in the protein folding process is the following: the first beta-hairpin, the first beta-helix, the second beta-helix, and the second beta-hairpin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the order of formation and the stability of beta-hairpin elements are not identical.
the μ-analysis approach allows determining the order of formation for structural elements in the process of multi-state protein folding and, in particular, for the formation of beta-hairs in GFP.
the μ-analysis approach can be used to study the order of formation and the structure of intermediate states of multi-state proteins.
